title: Marcos Vows 'We Do Not Yield' to China in State of the Nation Address
detail: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. pledged to defend the Philippines' South China Sea rights in his State of the Nation Address to Congress on July 27, 2026, declaring "We are Filipinos, and we do not yield." The remarks, made days after Manila condemned a China Daily video depicting Filipinos as monkeys and amid a week of maritime clashes at Second Thomas and Scarborough shoals, reaffirmed the 2016 Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling that invalidated China's nine-dash line claim over most of the South China Sea. Marcos's speech carried added weight given the string of recent Chinese Coast Guard confrontations with Philippine vessels.

media.caption: President Marcos pledges 'we do not yield' to China in his State of the Nation Address

title: Trump Assures Marcos Philippines' South China Sea Concerns Will Be Raised With Xi
detail: US President Donald Trump told President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in a phone call around July 27, 2026 that the Philippines' South China Sea concerns would be "taken up" with Chinese President Xi Jinping, following a week of Chinese Coast Guard clashes with Philippine vessels at Second Thomas and Scarborough shoals. The call reaffirmed the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty relationship amid the Marcos administration's push for stronger allied backing against Chinese maritime pressure.

media.caption: Trump assures Marcos: PH's South China Sea concerns to be 'taken up' with Xi

title: USS George Washington Carrier Strike Group Patrols Tension-Filled South China Sea
detail: The US Navy deployed the aircraft carrier strike group led by USS George Washington and its embarked F-35 squadrons to patrol the South China Sea, reported July 27, 2026, amid the week's clashes between China and the Philippines. The US Ambassador to the Philippines said the carrier group was "upholding freedom of navigation and overflight in the South China Sea," underscoring continued American naval presence alongside the Philippines, Japan, and Australia in the contested waterway.

media.caption: USS George Washington carrier strike group patrols the tension-filled South China Sea
